title: What Phlebotomists Do
description: Phlebotomists draw blood for testing, transfusions, and donation. They verify patient identity, select veins, perform venipuncture or capillary sticks, label specimens at the bedside, and transport them to the lab. They work in hospitals, clinics, labs, and blood-donation centers — the first link in the diagnostic chain.
key_points: First link in the diagnostic chain
Venipuncture, capillary sticks, and donation draws
Bedside labeling — never away from the patient
how_it_works: Select and prepare the venipuncture site
Perform the draw with correct technique
Label at bedside and transport properly
requirements: High school diploma; accredited phlebotomy program or on-the-job training
National certification (ASCP, NHA, AMT) preferred by most employers
standards: CLSI venipuncture procedures as the practice standard
Correct order of draw for multi-tube collections
Two patient identifiers before every draw
Proper labeling at the bedside before leaving the patient
safety: Standard precautions and gloves for every draw
Never recap needles; activate safety devices immediately
Sharps containers within arm's reach
Manage vasovagal reactions: recline, cool cloth, monitor
troubleshooting: No blood flow: check needle position, re-anchor the vein
Collapsed vein: release tourniquet, choose a new site
Hematoma forming: remove needle, apply firm pressure
Patient faints: stop the draw, lower the head, stay with them
citations: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute venipuncture guidance; American Society for Clinical Pathology resources; phlebotomy clinical textbooks.
provenance: Public trade knowledge drawn from phlebotomy education, professional association guidance, and clinical laboratory references. Real, fact-checked records.

title: Venipuncture Technique
description: The core skill: anchor the vein with the non-dominant hand, insert the needle bevel-up at 15-30 degrees, and watch for flashback. Anchor firmly — veins roll. Fill tubes in order of draw, release the tourniquet before withdrawing, and apply pressure with gauze. Smooth, confident, one stick.

title: Capillary Collection
description: Finger and heel sticks serve patients with fragile veins — infants, elderly, and burn patients. Warm the site, puncture with a single deliberate lancet motion, wipe away the first drop, and collect free-flowing drops without squeezing (squeezing hemolyzes the sample). Different site, same precision standard.
